title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Rule on Backdating the Claim Effective Date
content:
**(1)** A claimant of Unemployment Benefit Claims who did not file in the first week of unemployment may ask to move the claim effective date earlier.

**(2)** Backdating is available only for programs whose maximum backdating weeks is above zero, for no more weeks than that maximum, and only with good cause recorded on the backdate request, being one of: illness or injury; agency error; employer misinformation; natural disaster; death in family.

**(3)** A backdating request is accepted only when it is lodged no later than the backdating request window after the requested effective date. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the requested effective date, and a request on the last day is in time. The requested effective date read is the one recorded on the backdate request.

**(4)** The new effective date is always a Sunday, and the benefit year end date moves with it.

**(5)** Backdating does not change the monetary determination unless the earlier effective date changes the base period, in which case a monetary redetermination is issued.

**(6)** Weeks brought into the claim by backdating must still be certified and are payable only under the ordinary weekly rules.

## Both sides of the request window (a 60-day window)

| Day the request is lodged, counted from the day after the requested effective date | Request window |
|---|---|
| Day 60 | In time |
| Day 61 | Too late |

## Conditions together

| Program's maximum backdating weeks above zero | Weeks requested within the maximum | Good cause from the listed reasons recorded | Lodged within the window | Request accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | — | — | — | No |
| Yes | No | — | — | No |
| Yes | Yes | No | — | No |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No |
